sourcedFrom: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code (ABSENT)
cleanIntro: The Trojan is STI's single-stack 1911, and STI publishes ONE takedown for its whole 1911/2011 line. Two things are worth knowing before you start. STI's disassembly section opens with a SIX-INCH-ONLY procedure for a two-piece guide rod, and most STI handguns — the Trojan among them — use a ONE-PIECE rod instead, so the first steps on the page are probably not yours. And the one-piece removal needs a tool STI expects you to make from a paper clip. Read the whole procedure before starting; the maker says so in his own words.

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine and chamber first, goggles on, then READ the whole procedure
steps.action: Remove the magazine and any round in the chamber before anything else, and put safety goggles on — this strip releases a spring under compression. Then read STI's disassembly section through before starting. Work on a clean, lint-free cloth with room to lay parts out in order.
steps.prose: The instruction to read it all first is in the manual because the guide-rod step is not one to discover halfway through.
steps.aside: Read through the entire disassembly procedure before attempting to disassemble any of the STI model handguns.
steps.quote: Always remove the magazine and any ammunition in the firearm’s chamber before disassembly.
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Handgun maintenance: disassembly, printed p.22

steps.title: ⚠ Check which guide rod you have BEFORE following the first page
steps.action: STI's disassembly section opens with a two-piece guide rod procedure marked for 6-inch guns only, and notes that most STI models have a one-piece guide rod assembly. Look at your own gun: if there is no hex head under the muzzle, you have the one-piece system and the two-piece steps are not yours.
steps.prose: A procedure printed first is not a procedure that applies first. This is the one place in the book where reading straight down the page will mislead you.
steps.caution: Contact STI International for further clarification or instructions should any of the parts or assemblies shown in the disassembly process of this manual appear different from those found on your STI model.
steps.quote: Most STI models have a one piece guide rod
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Two piece guide rod removal, printed p.23

steps.title: Slide back to the SECOND notch from the muzzle, aligned with the slide stop
steps.action: Hold the frame by the grip, grasp the slide at the rear and draw it back until the disassembly notch — the second notch from the muzzle end — lines up with the rear of the slide stop on the left side. Keep the alignment and keep a firm grip; do not let the slide run forward.
steps.prose: The second notch, not the first. The first is the slide-lock notch and it will not release the stop.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back until the disassembly notch on the slide (the second notch from the muzzle end) aligns with the rear of the slide stop on the left-hand side of the handgun.
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Slide stop removal, printed p.24

steps.title: Slide stop out by pushing on its RIGHT-hand extended portion
steps.action: With the notch still aligned, push against the extended portion of the slide stop on the RIGHT-hand side of the pistol and draw the stop out to the left. STI notes the stop has to be pushed down into its lowest position before it will come out. Once it is clear you can release the slide pressure.
steps.prose: Pushing from the wrong side just pinches the stop against the frame and marks the finish.
steps.aside: The slide stop must be pushed down into its lowest position before it can be removed.
steps.quote: While maintaining the slide disassembly notch alignment with the slide stop, remove the slide stop by pushing against the extended portion of the stop, located on the right-hand side of the handgun.
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Slide stop removal, printed p.24

steps.title: ⛔ Slide assembly forward off the frame — eye protection ON
steps.action: Keeping a firm grip, run the slide assembly forward off the front of the frame and set the frame aside. STI puts an explicit eye-protection caution at this step because the next one may release a spring under compression.
steps.prose: The recoil spring becomes exposed at the underside of the slide as it comes forward. That is the moment to have already put the goggles on.
steps.caution: CAUTION: Wear eye protection! The next step might require the removal of a spring under compression.
steps.quote: Remove the slide assembly from the handgun frame
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Slide assembly removal, printed p.25

steps.title: One-piece recoil system: capture it with a bent paper clip
steps.action: Turn the slide over to expose the barrel and recoil system. STI's own method is to straighten a paper clip and put a 90° bend about 0.100" long in one end. Push the guide rod head with your thumb to compress the spring; when a small hole appears in the front of the guide rod, hook the tool into it and ease the spring pressure off until the tool has captured the reverse plug. Draw the captured assembly out toward the rear of the slide — and leave it captured, because that is how it goes back in.
steps.prose: Larger calibres have heavier springs and are harder to compress. Work slowly; STI says this step takes practice.
steps.aside: Note: with larger caliber firearms the recoil spring will be heavier thus making it harder to compress.
steps.quote: With your thumb push on the guide rod head thus compressing the recoil spring. When a small hole appears in the front of the guide rod, insert the “hook” into the hole. Slowly release recoil spring pressure until the tool has captured the reverse plug. The captured system will be removed by pulling the guide rod head towards the rear of the slide.
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — One piece guide rod removal, printed p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete — and know when to stop
steps.action: Slide, frame, barrel and the captured recoil assembly. STI takes the owner further in the same section — firing pin, extractor — but flags that the procedures need manual dexterity and specific tools and to seek a qualified gunsmith if you are unsure. For routine cleaning, this is far enough.
steps.prose: A maker who tells you to stop if you are unsure has told you something useful about the step that follows.
steps.quote: The following disassembly procedure requires manual dexterity and specific tools. Seek the service of a qualified gunsmith for assistance if you are uncertain of your ability to perform the following disassembly process.
steps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Handgun maintenance: disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: ⛔ No brake cleaner, no grease
deepSteps.action: STI names both by name in its own supplies list: a high-quality cleaning solvent, explicitly not brake cleaner, and high-quality gun oil, explicitly not grease. Brake cleaner strips the finish and everything else with it; grease in a 1911's rails collects grit and holds it against the bearing surfaces.
deepSteps.prose: Two products that are cheap, close to hand, and specifically excluded.
deepSteps.quote: High-Quality Cleaning Solvent (Do not use brake cleaner)
deepSteps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Handgun maintenance: cleaning, printed p.34

deepSteps.title: The rails are the job on a 1911
deepSteps.action: Scrub powder residue off the slide rails and the frame rails specifically, with a nylon brush and solvent, then wipe with lint-free cotton and inspect for damage or unusual wear. On a tightly-fitted 1911 the rails are where fit lives, and where fouling changes how the gun runs.
deepSteps.prose: Inspect while it is clean. Wear shows on bare metal, not through carbon.
deepSteps.quote: Clean slide using a nylon brush and cleaning solvent; scrub away any powder residue, particularly on the slide rails.
deepSteps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Cleaning instructions, printed p.34

deepSteps.title: ⚠ If your parts do not look like the book's, ask before you force anything
deepSteps.action: This is a category manual covering the whole STI 1911 and 2011 line, and STI says so: if any part or assembly shown in the disassembly process looks different from what is on your gun, contact them for clarification rather than proceeding.
deepSteps.prose: That instruction is the honest edge of a one-book-many-models manual, and it is worth taking literally.
deepSteps.quote: Contact STI International for further clarification or instructions should any of the parts or assemblies shown in the disassembly process of this manual appear different from those found on your STI model.
deepSteps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — Handgun maintenance: disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: The recoil assembly goes back the way it came out — captured
deepSteps.action: Keep the paper-clip tool in the reverse plug while the assembly is out of the gun. It is reinstalled captured and the tool comes out last, after the assembly is seated. Releasing it on the bench means compressing it again against nothing to hold it.
deepSteps.prose: STI's own words are 'keep the system captured for installation'.
deepSteps.quote: With your thumb push on the guide rod head thus compressing the recoil spring. When a small hole appears in the front of the guide rod, insert the “hook” into the hole. Slowly release recoil spring pressure until the tool has captured the reverse plug. The captured system will be removed by pulling the guide rod head towards the rear of the slide.
deepSteps.cite: ALL STI 1911 & 2011 FIREARMS — HANDGUN SAFETY REFERENCE & OWNER'S MANUAL — undated — the book carries no edition or revision code — One piece guide rod removal, printed p.23

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BORE
tasks: Bronze bore brush on a threaded cleaning rod to lift heavy deposits, then a slotted tip with 100% cotton flannel patches until they come out clean.
Wipe the outside of the barrel and the lugs; inspect for wear.

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Nylon brush and solvent on the slide, scrubbing powder residue off particularly the SLIDE RAILS; wipe with lint-free cotton and inspect.
Same on the frame, particularly the FRAME RAILS.
⛔ High-quality solvent only — STI says do not use brake cleaner.

cleaning.name: RECOIL SYSTEM
tasks: Wipe the captured guide-rod assembly down without dismantling it; it goes back captured.
⛔ Gun oil, not grease — STI names grease as something not to use.

reassembly: Captured recoil assembly back into the slide, still captured, then release the tool.
Barrel into the slide, then the slide assembly onto the frame rails.
Draw the slide back to the SECOND notch and align it with the slide stop hole.
Slide stop in from the left, pressed down to its lowest position as it enters.
Ease the slide forward and confirm it runs fully into battery.
⛔ Function-check before the pistol goes away.
fncheck: With the pistol CLEAR: check the thumb safety engages and blocks the trigger, and that the grip safety must be depressed before the trigger will move. Cycle the slide several times and watch it return fully to battery under spring pressure alone. With the gun empty and pointed safely, pull the trigger for a clean break; hold it back, cycle the slide, release and listen for the reset. Insert an EMPTY magazine and confirm the slide locks back on the slide stop.
